name: Edmond H. Fischer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; PhD completed in 1947 at age 27, Nobel-winning protein phosphorylation discovery came in 1955-56 at age 35-36.
early_history_summary: Sent to Swiss boarding school at age 7, studied at University of Geneva during WWII, completing a PhD in organic chemistry in 1947 under Kurt Heinrich Meyer. Postdoctoral research at University of Washington began in 1950 at age 30.
family_context_summary: Father was a lawyer in Shanghai; maternal grandfather founded a French newspaper in China. Family was well-off enough to send children to Swiss boarding school.
evidence_summary: Fischer completed his PhD at age 27, after which he moved to the University of Washington. His Nobel Prize-winning discovery of reversible protein phosphorylation with Edwin Krebs occurred in the mid-1950s when he was in his mid-30s. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Miloš Forman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; first feature film 'Black Peter' released in 1964 at age 32, breakthrough came with 'Loves of a Blonde' (1965) and 'The Firemen's Ball' (1967).
early_history_summary: Orphaned during WWII (father died in Buchenwald, mother murdered in Auschwitz). Raised by uncles and family friends. Attended boarding school in Poděbrady with Václav Havel and Ivan Passer, then studied screenwriting at the Academy of Performing Arts in Prague (FAMU). Was assistant to Alfréd Radok before his directorial career began in the early 1960s.
family_context_summary: Parents killed during Nazi occupation; father was in Czech Resistance, mother murdered in Auschwitz. Raised by uncles and family friends after becoming an orphan.
evidence_summary: Forman studied screenwriting at FAMU and worked as assistant to Alfréd Radok, but his first feature film 'Black Peter' did not come until 1964 when he was 32. No material directorial milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Daniel Passarella
milestone_by_age_26: Joined River Plate, one of Argentina's biggest clubs, in 1973 at age 20; debuted for Argentina national team in March 1976 at age 22; named Argentine Footballer of the Year in 1976; won multiple league titles (1975 Metropolitano, 1975 Nacional) by age 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Chacabuco, Buenos Aires. Started career at Sarmiento de Junín in 1971 at age 18, scoring 9 goals in 36 appearances. Joined River Plate in 1973, where he became a prolific scoring defender and was called up to the Argentina national team. By age 23 he was named Argentine Footballer of the Year and had won two league titles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: River Plate pipeline, Argentine football culture, early professional debut, prolific scoring defender
evidence_summary: Passarella started his professional career at Sarmiento in 1971 at age 18 and joined River Plate in 1973 at age 20, quickly becoming a key player. He debuted for Argentina in March 1976 at age 22 and was named Argentine Footballer of the Year that same year. He won the 1975 Metropolitano and Nacional titles with River Plate. His family background is not documented in reviewed sources. His rise through the Argentine football pipeline from a provincial club to River Plate and the national team by his early 20s represents a clear elite performance pipeline trajectory.

name: John Woo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; worked as script supervisor (1969) and assistant director (1971) but directorial debut 'The Young Dragons' came in 1974 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Born in Guangzhou, China, fled to Hong Kong at age 5. Grew up impoverished in slums, family rendered homeless by Shek Kip Mei Fire of 1953. Inspired by French New Wave and American Westerns. Hired as script supervisor at Cathay Studios in 1969, became assistant director at Shaw Studios in 1971 under Chang Cheh.
family_context_summary: Family was impoverished; father was a teacher incapacitated by tuberculosis, mother was a manual laborer. Family fled communist China to Hong Kong when Woo was 5, rendered homeless by fire in 1953.
evidence_summary: Woo entered the Hong Kong film industry as a script supervisor at Cathay Studios in 1969 and became an assistant director at Shaw Studios in 1971, but his directorial debut did not come until 1974 at age 28. His apprenticeship roles before 26 do not constitute a material independently verifiable milestone.

name: Jon Voight
milestone_by_age_26: Made Broadway debut in fall 1961 as Rolf in 'The Sound of Music' at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre at age 22, and continued working in off-Broadway and television through his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Raised in Yonkers, New York, by a professional golfer father. Attended Archbishop Stepinac High School where he first took interest in acting, then Catholic University of America (BA in art, 1960). Moved to New York City and studied at the Neighborhood Playhouse under Sanford Meisner. Made off-Broadway debut in 'O Oysters' (early 1961) and Broadway debut in 'The Sound of Music' (fall 1961).
family_context_summary: Father was a professional golfer; brother Barry Voight is a volcanologist, brother Chip Taylor is a singer-songwriter. Middle-class upbringing in Yonkers, New York.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct family domain advantage in acting, but family had notable achievement across diverse fields (golf, science, music).
primary_early_advantage_tags: Neighborhood Playhouse training, Broadway pipeline, New York theater ecosystem, Meisner technique
evidence_summary: Voight graduated from Catholic University in 1960, studied under Sanford Meisner at the Neighborhood Playhouse, and made his Broadway debut in 'The Sound of Music' in fall 1961 at age 22. His father was a professional golfer and his brothers achieved distinction in science and music, suggesting a supportive, achievement-oriented family environment. The New York theater ecosystem and Meisner training provided the institutional pipeline for his early career. His breakthrough film role in 'Midnight Cowboy' (1969) came later, but the Broadway debut by 22 is a material milestone.

name: Joe Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; worked as a steelworker and briefly performed in a blues band (The Falcons, disbanded 1952) but talent management career began in the 1960s at age 36 with the Jackson 5.
early_history_summary: Born in Fountain Hill, Arkansas. Parents separated when he was 12; moved to Oakland with father, then to East Chicago at 18. Worked at Inland Steel Company, pursued boxing in Golden Gloves. In early 1950s, briefly played guitar in blues band The Falcons with his brother, but the band did not secure a recording contract and disbanded in 1952. Married Katherine Scruse in 1949.
family_context_summary: Father was a teacher; parents separated when he was 12. Grew up in working-class circumstances, did not finish high school, worked as a steelworker.
evidence_summary: Joe Jackson worked as a steelworker and briefly played in a blues band that failed to secure a recording contract. His career as a talent manager began in the 1960s when he was in his mid-30s, managing his sons as the Jackson 5. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: László Kubala
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for Ferencváros at age 18 in 1945, scoring 27 goals in 49 games; played for Czechoslovakia national team (1946-47) at age 19; signed for FC Barcelona in June 1950 at age 23; won Copa del Generalísimo with Barcelona in 1951 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest to working-class parents (father a bricklayer, mother a factory worker). Began playing youth football at Ganz TE at age 11 with older players. Signed for Ferencváros at 18, then moved to Slovan Bratislava in 1946. Fled communist Hungary in 1949 as a refugee, formed his own team Hungaria with fellow refugees, and was signed by Barcelona in 1950 after being spotted by José Samitier.
family_context_summary: Father was a bricklayer, mother was a factory worker with Polish and Slovak roots. Working-class family in Budapest. Brother-in-law Ferdinand Daučík was a football coach who became Barcelona coach alongside Kubala.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct family football domain advantage, but brother-in-law Ferdinand Daučík was Czechoslovak national coach and later Barcelona coach, providing a significant professional connection.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Early professional debut, refugee displacement, Ferencváros pipeline, Barcelona signing, brother-in-law coach connection
evidence_summary: Kubala was playing senior football by age 17 and signed for Ferencváros at 18, one of Hungary's top clubs. He represented Czechoslovakia internationally at 19 and was signed by Barcelona at 23 after fleeing communist Hungary as a refugee. His brother-in-law Ferdinand Daučík was a national team coach who accompanied him to Barcelona. The adversity of wartime and Cold War displacement shaped his peripatetic early career, but his exceptional talent was recognized from a young age. By 26 he had won the Copa del Generalísimo with Barcelona.

name: Tomas Lindahl
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; PhD completed in 1967 at age 29, MD in 1970 at age 32, Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2015 at age 77.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockholm, Sweden. Studied at the Karolinska Institutet, receiving a PhD in 1967 and an MD qualification in 1970. Postdoctoral research at Princeton and Rockefeller University followed. His pioneering work on DNA repair came later in his career.
family_context_summary: Born to Folke Robert Lindahl and Ethel Hulda Hultberg in Stockholm. Not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Lindahl was still a student at the Karolinska Institutet at age 26, with his PhD not completed until 1967 at age 29. His Nobel Prize-winning work on DNA repair came decades later. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Yayoi Kusama
milestone_by_age_26: Held first solo exhibition in March 1952 at age 23 at Matsumoto's First Community Centre, featuring over 200 artworks; held a second solo exhibition in September 1952; staged multiple solo exhibitions in Matsumoto and Tokyo through the 1950s.
early_history_summary: Born in Matsumoto, Nagano, to a family that owned a plant nursery and seed farm. Began drawing from hallucinations in elementary school. Sent to work in a military factory at age 13 during WWII. Studied Nihonga painting at Kyoto Municipal School of Arts and Crafts from 1948, but became frustrated with traditional style and gravitated toward European and American avant-garde. Held first solo exhibition in 1952 at age 23.
family_context_summary: Born into a prosperous family that owned a plant nursery and seed farm with a greenhouse, a rarity at the time. Mother was physically abusive and unsupportive of her creative endeavors; father was described as a womanizer.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct art domain advantage from family; family business was in plant nursery and seeds. Mother actively discouraged artistic pursuits.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hallucinatory visions, traumatic childhood, early solo exhibitions, avant-garde connections, obsessive production
evidence_summary: Kusama held her first solo exhibition at age 23 in March 1952, featuring over 200 artworks created in just a few months. Born into a prosperous plant nursery family, she experienced a traumatic childhood with an abusive mother and vivid hallucinations that became the source of her distinctive artistic style. She studied Nihonga at Kyoto but rebelled toward avant-garde, connecting with art critic Shūzō Takiguchi. Her work came to the attention of psychiatrists Dr. Shiho Nishimaru and Dr. Ryuzaburo Shikiba. By 26 she had staged multiple solo exhibitions in Matsumoto and Tokyo.

name: Michael Caine
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; had minor credited film and TV roles by 1959 but breakthrough came with 'Zulu' (1964) at age 31 and stardom with 'The Ipcress File' (1965) and 'Alfie' (1966).
early_history_summary: Born in Rotherhithe, London to a charwoman and fish market porter. Evacuated during WWII, made stage debut at village school in Norfolk. Left school at 16, worked as filing clerk. Film debut (uncredited) in 'Morning Departure' (1950). National service 1951-53 including Korean War. Joined repertory theater in 1953, moved to London in 1954. First film role in 'A Hill in Korea' (1956), first credited BBC role in 1956. Described his first nine years as 'really, really brutal.'
family_context_summary: Working-class background in London; father was a fish market porter, mother was a cook and charwoman. Grew up in Southwark, evacuated during WWII. Father from an Irish Traveller Catholic family.
evidence_summary: Caine had minor credited film and TV roles by age 26, including 'A Hill in Korea' (1956) and BBC appearances, and was an understudy to Peter O'Toole in a West End production in 1959. However, these were bit parts and journeyman work; his own description of his first nine years as 'really, really brutal' confirms the absence of a material milestone. His breakthrough came with 'Zulu' (1964) at age 31.

name: Heinrich Rohrer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was still a PhD student at ETH Zurich working on cryogenic engineering, with PhD completed later. Joined IBM Research in 1963 at age 30; Nobel Prize for STM in 1986 at age 53.
early_history_summary: Born in Buchs, St. Gallen, Switzerland. Enjoyed a carefree country childhood until family moved to Zurich in 1949. Enrolled at ETH (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology) in 1951, studying under Wolfgang Pauli and Paul Scherrer. PhD thesis on cryogenic engineering supervised by P. Grassmann. Studies interrupted by Swiss military service. Postdoc at Rutgers University in 1961, joined IBM Research in 1963.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond mention of a twin sister and a carefree country childhood.
evidence_summary: Rohrer enrolled at ETH in 1951 and was still working on his PhD at age 26, with his studies interrupted by military service. His postdoc at Rutgers came in 1961 at age 28, and he joined IBM Research in 1963. The scanning tunneling microscope was developed in the 1980s. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Franco Zeffirelli
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; worked as assistant director to Luchino Visconti on 'La Terra trema' (released 1948) but first film as director was 'The Taming of the Shrew' (1967) at age 44, and first opera directing work came in the 1950s.
early_history_summary: Born in Florence, Italy, to an unmarried couple (a fashion designer and a wool/silk dealer). Mother died when he was 6; grew up under the English expatriate community (the 'Scorpioni'). Graduated from Accademia di Belle Arti Firenze in 1941, studied art and architecture at University of Florence. Fought as a partisan in WWII, then served as interpreter for British soldiers. After seeing Laurence Olivier's 'Henry V' in 1945, turned to theatre. Worked as scene painter, then assistant director to Visconti.
family_context_summary: Born out of an affair between a fashion designer and a wool/silk dealer. Mother died when he was 6. Grew up connected to the English expatriate community in Florence. Found to be a descendant of Leonardo da Vinci's family.
evidence_summary: Zeffirelli worked as an assistant director to Luchino Visconti on 'La Terra trema' (1948) and with De Sica and Rossellini, but his own directorial debut did not come until 'The Taming of the Shrew' (1967) at age 44. His opera directing career began in the 1950s. The assistant director role before 26 is an apprenticeship position, not a material independently verifiable milestone.
